submission.justification: Provisional recommendation: Sensor-T2 (thin-pitch, large signal sharing) at 150 um. It gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution of the nine technology/thickness points simulated (6.224 um, versus 6.909 um at 50 um and 7.840 um at 300 um for T2; T1 best is 9.140 um and T3 best is 13.710 um). T2 is best at every thickness, and 150 um is the best thickness for every technology. The radiation constraint is NOT verified. No project document gives a fluence or dose requirement at the innermost radius, and the simulation does not model irradiated performance, so radiation suitability of all three technologies is unknown and none could be excluded. The stated goal is best resolution, so 150 um is chosen, but this choice should be treated as conditional. If irradiated simulations or the fluence requirement show charge-collection loss at 150 um, the fallback is T2 at 50 um (6.909 um unirradiated, about 0.7 um worse). Thickness was sampled at only three points per technology, so the true optimum between 50 and 300 um is not resolved. Before final sign-off, obtain the innermost-layer fluence requirement and simulate irradiated resolution for T2 at 50 and 150 um.

[s5 summary] **Recommendation (provisional): Sensor-T2 (thin-pitch, large signal sharing) at 150 µm.** This is not a fully validated submission. The radiation constraint is unverified.

**Supporting resolution numbers (unirradiated, single-hit, from the simulation):**

| Technology | 50 µm | 150 µm | 300 µm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sensor-T1 | 10.631 | 9.140 | 11.625 |
| **Sensor-T2** | 6.909 | **6.224** | 7.840 |
| Sensor-T3 | 16.791 | 13.710 | 19.633 |

Sensor-T2 is the best technology at every thickness, and 150 µm is the best thickness for every technology. T2 at 150 µm gives the best resolution of the nine points tested.

**Radiation justification: not established.** The project documents contain no fluence or dose requirement for the innermost layer, no irradiated resolution data, and no radiation-tolerance information. I therefore could not confirm or exclude any technology on radiation grounds, which is a stated constraint. The only basis for a thickness choice is general sensor physics: charge-collection loss at high fluence usually favours thinner sensors. On that basis, T2 at 50 µm is the safer fallback. It costs about 0.7 µm of resolution (6.909 vs 6.224 µm) and is the better choice if irradiated simulations penalise 150 µm.

**Caveats:**
- All resolution numbers are for unirradiated sensors. The simulation tool does not model irradiation, so the innermost-layer performance is unknown.
- Thickness was sampled at only three points per technology. The true optimum between 50 and 300 µm is not resolved.
- Before final sign-off, the project needs to supply the fluence requirement at the innermost radius. Irradiated resolution should then be simulated for T2 at 50 µm and 150 µm, and the choice made from those results.
